messages.content: What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?

function.name: locate_tallest_mountains
function.description: Find the tallest mountains within a specified radius of a location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city from which to calculate distance.

radius.description: The radius within which to find mountains, measured in kilometers. This is a float type value.

amount.description: The number of mountains to find, listed from tallest to smallest.

function.name: calculate_electric_field
function.description: Calculate the electric field produced by a charge at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge.description: Charge in coulombs producing the electric field. This is a float type value.

distance.description: Distance from the charge in meters where the field is being measured. This is a float type value.

permitivity.description: Permitivity of the space where field is being calculated, default is for vacuum. This is a float type value.

function.name: calculate_genotype_frequency
function.description: Calculate the frequency of homozygous dominant genotype based on the allele frequency using Hardy Weinberg Principle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

allele_frequency.description: The frequency of the dominant allele in the population. This is a float type value.

genotype.description: The genotype which frequency is needed, default is homozygous dominant.

function.name: cellbio_get_proteins

include_description.description: Set true if you want a brief description of each protein.

message.content:
**Proteins that are commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often serve as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, muscarinic acetylcholine receptor
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** – e.g., epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)
• **Ion channels** – e.g., voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv), calcium channel (Cav)
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels)
• **Integrins** (cell‑matrix adhesion)
• **Cadherins** (cell‑cell adhesion) | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface (inner or outer leaflet) via electrostatic or lipid‑anchor interactions. | • **Actin** (cytoskeletal support)
• **Spectrin** (membrane skeleton)
• **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to the cytoskeleton)
• **Protein kinase C** (signal transduction)
• **Src family kinases** (membrane‑associated signaling)
• **Glycophorin A** (outer leaflet, erythrocyte membrane) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., GPI anchors) and remain on the outer leaflet. | • **GPI‑anchored CD59** (protects cells from complement)
• **GPI‑anchored CD55 (decay‑accelerating factor)**
• **GPI‑anchored prion protein (PrP^C)** | | **Other specialized proteins** | Serve unique roles such as cell‑surface recognition or immune function. | • **MHC class I & II molecules** (antigen presentation)
• **Toll‑like receptors** (innate immunity)
• **Neurotransmitter receptors** – e.g., NMDA receptor, AMPA receptor | These proteins together give the plasma membrane its selective permeability, signaling capabilities, structural integrity, and interaction with the extracellular environment. The exact composition varies between cell types and physiological conditions.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They want a list of proteins found in the plasma membrane. We can provide a general answer: types of proteins: integral membrane proteins (e.g., ion channels, transporters, receptors), peripheral membrane proteins (e.g., cytoskeletal proteins, signaling proteins). Provide examples: e.g., Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptors like β-adrenergic receptor, integrins, cadherins, connexins, etc. Also mention peripheral proteins: actin, spectrin, ankyrin, etc. Provide a concise list. No function calls needed.
